function: Channel estimation with adaptive pilot design by a DNN in a THz massive MIMO-OFDM ISAC system; positioning then follows by non-learned tensor decomposition (pp. 3, 5).
system: THz massive MIMO-OFDM at 300 GHz; BS and MS each with an 8x8 UPA and hybrid precoding; 128 subcarriers, 3 for training; NLoS paths; no RIS (pp. 4, 9).
method: Autoencoder-principle DNN trained offline end to end with MSE against the true channel: FC compression layer, FC layer, 8 convolutional refinement units; then non-learned CP/ALS (pp. 5-6, 9).
data_channel: Authors' own simulated channel, Eq. (1) with SFW effect: L=3 NLoS paths, random angles, delay 0-1 ns, Gaussian gains; 2000 training, 1000 validation, 500 test groups (pp. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same simulated model (500 held-out groups); sweeps over SNR 0-20 dB, compression ratio 0.125-0.625, path number L=2-4; no unseen scenario stated (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned OMP [14], SOMP [15], AMP [42] (called conventional, p. 9), each feeding the same tensor and positioning stages; no learned estimator compared (p. 9).
metrics: Channel NMSE (dB); RMSE of AoA, AoD, delay, path gain, and of MS and scattering-point positions (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "a channel dataset is generated, which is based on the model scenario described in Section II-A". That model is the authors' own geometric THz channel (Eq. 1, p. 4) with random angles, delays and Gaussian gains; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "2000 groups for the training set" and "500 groups for the test set", both from the one generated dataset. The sweeps over SNR (p. 9), compression ratio (p. 11), and path number (p. 12) are not stated as train-test mismatches; no unseen scenario or adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 9: "we compare it with the existing CS and iterative algorithms, including the OMP algorithm [14], the SOMP algorithm [15], and the AMP algorithm [42]"; p. 11 calls them "traditional algorithms". No earlier learned estimator or standard network (CNN, FC) is compared, so only the non-learned side is met.
q4_support: p. 2: "With its strong approximation ability and low-computational complexity, deep learning (DL)" is a generic claim about DL. No order of complexity, operations, parameter count, or runtime of the proposed method is reported; p. 9 gives only 8 refinement units and a Tesla T4 GPU.
q5_support: p. 9: "a channel dataset is generated, which is based on the model scenario described in Section II-A". The data are the authors' own simulation; no code or data link is given and no public dataset is used.
notes: Included, area 2: the DNN performs channel estimation and pilot design (p. 5) in an ISAC system, which the instructions place in area 2 (channel estimation in ISAC), not area 5. Positioning is a later non-learned stage (CP/ALS tensor decomposition and weighted least squares, pp. 6-8), so the localization exclusion does not apply. The SNR used to train the DNN is not stated. For the reviewer on q3: reference [42] is He et al., "Deep learning-based channel estimation for beamspace mmWave massive MIMO systems" (p. 15), a learned network, but the paper calls AMP "conventional" (p. 9) and "traditional" (p. 11) and compares no other learned estimator, so q3 is 0; check whether the AMP baseline is that learned network.
